commands.name: checkout-sessions
commands.description: Hosted checkout pages, where a customer signs up and pays.

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates a checkout session and returns a browser-safe session token plus a hosted checkout URL. Embed the URL with the Alguna Checkout SDK, or redirect the customer to it directly. The session charges a plan's prices, ad-hoc line items, or a bare amount, and expires after `expires_in_seconds`.
methods.epilogue:
Example:
  alguna checkout-sessions create --customer-id cus_123 --plan-id plan_123 --success-url https://example.com/done

options.name: amount
options.description: Total amount to charge when neither plan_id nor line_items are provided

options.name: checkout-intent
options.description: payment charges the customer; vault only collects and stores a payment method. Defaults to payment.

options.name: client-reference-id
options.description: Your own reference for this checkout (order ID, cart ID). Echoed on the session and the checkout.session.completed webhook.

options.name: currency
options.description: ISO 4217 currency code; defaults to the organization currency

options.name: customer-alias
options.description: Alternative identifier (external ID) for the customer. Used when customer_id is not provided.

options.name: customer-id
options.description: Customer the checkout is for. Omit for guest checkout and pass customer instead — the customer account is created when checkout completes.

options.name: expires-in-seconds
options.description: Session lifetime in seconds (5 minutes to 7 days). Defaults to 86400 (24 hours).

options.name: legal-entity-id
options.description: Legal entity to bill from. Defaults to the customer's legal entity, falling back to the organization default.

options.name: plan-id
options.description: Plan to check out. The session's line items and amount are derived from the plan's prices. Mutually exclusive with line_items.

options.name: success-url
options.description: URL the customer can be sent to after a successful checkout

methods.name: get
methods.description: Returns the current state of a checkout session, including the payment and subscription it created once the customer completes checkout. Poll this endpoint or subscribe to the `checkout.session.completed` webhook event.

commands.name: credit-notes
commands.description: Credit notes, which credit or refund all or part of an invoice.

methods.name: list
methods.description: Returns a paginated list of credit notes for a given customer. The `customer_id` query parameter is required.

options.name: customer-id
options.description: Customer ID to list credit notes for

options.name: limit
options.description: Number of items to return per page

options.name: offset
options.description: Number of items to skip

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates a credit note in draft status. Optionally link it to an invoice. Linked paid invoices are supported, and pre-payment credit notes are supported for Alguna-managed invoices in `issued` or `overdue`. Add line items to specify the credited amounts, then apply the credit note to finalize it. Alternatively, set `apply` to create and apply the credit note in one call — the same synchronous flow as calling Apply Credit Note on a draft. Applying alone does not return funds; send `refund` as well to refund the customer, which requires a linked invoice that is paid. If applying fails, the credit note is left in draft and the error identifies it so it can be applied separately.

options.name: apply
options.description: Apply the credit note as part of creating it, synchronously, exactly as create followed by Apply Credit Note would. Defaults to false, leaving it a draft. If applying fails the credit note remains a draft and the error identifies it, so it can be retried via Apply Credit Note.

options.name: billing-period-end
options.description: End of the billing period

options.name: billing-period-start
options.description: Start of the billing period

options.name: customer-id
options.description: Customer the credit note is issued to. Required unless invoice_id is given, in which case it is taken from the invoice; when both are given they must agree.

options.name: description
options.description: Credit note description

options.name: invoice-id
options.description: Linked invoice. Required unless customer_id is given. Pre-payment credit notes are supported only for Alguna-managed invoices in issued or overdue

methods.name: get
methods.description: Fetches a single credit note by ID, including line items and attachments.

methods.name: apply
methods.description: Applies a draft credit note. Applying to a paid invoice can optionally trigger a refund to the original payment method or a wallet. Applying to an Alguna-managed invoice in `issued` or `overdue` records a pre-payment credit without issuing a refund. Once applied, the credit note cannot be modified.

options.name: do-refund
options.description: Whether to issue a refund when applying to a paid invoice

options.name: refund-destination
options.description: Where to send the refund when refunding a paid invoice

options.name: wallet-id
options.description: Wallet to refund to when refund_destination is wallet for a paid-invoice refund

methods.requireConfirmation: This operation applies the credit note, after which it cannot change, and can refund the customer.

methods.name: create-from-invoice
methods.description: Creates a draft credit note against an invoice, crediting it at the prices and tax it was issued with rather than calculating tax again. Omit `line_items` to credit everything still uncredited on the invoice. Give `line_items` to credit specific invoice lines, each by the `quantity` of units to credit, which may be fractional. Every line here credits an invoice line item; to credit an amount that is not on the invoice, use create-credit-note instead.

options.name: apply
options.description: Apply the credit note as part of creating it, synchronously, exactly as create followed by Apply Credit Note would. Defaults to false, leaving it a draft. If applying fails the credit note remains a draft and the error identifies it, so it can be retried via Apply Credit Note.

commands.name: credits
commands.description: Prepaid credit, reserved and charged for usage.

methods.name: check
methods.description:
Prices work before it happens and, optionally, reserves credit for it. The request carries no credit amount: describe the work as the events it will produce, and the response's `charges` say what it prices to per metric.

Send `events` alone to get a price with nothing recorded. Send `reserve` to open a hold, then close it with `POST /credits/track`. `"reserve": {}` with `events` holds enough for exactly that work; `"reserve": {"max_quantity": "100000"}` with `event_name` holds a ceiling in metric units. An `Idempotency-Key` is required whenever `reserve` is set. Each metric is held at the rate frozen when the hold opened, and the hold expires after 15 minutes unless `ttl_seconds` asks for longer (maximum 4 hours).

Only credit-gated metrics are accepted: an event feeding no credit-consuming metric is rejected with `422` and belongs on `POST /events`. Insufficient credit returns `200` with `allowed: false`; an `allowed: true` response carrying no `reservation_id` opened no hold.

The SDKs send no automatic `Idempotency-Key` on this call and retry it without one, because a price check records nothing. Send your own key only to open a hold, where it is required and identifies the hold, or to replay a specific response; a retry then sends the same key. The SDKs do not retry a `500`. `409` means the key is bound to a different reservation. Back off on `429`, which also covers a ledger at its concurrent-hold cap.
methods.epilogue:
Example:
  alguna credits check --account cus_123 --event-name api_call

options.name: account
options.description: Customer account ID or alias the credits belong to

options.name: event-name
options.description: The usage event the work will produce. This is what resolves which billable metrics the check is against — you name what you are about to do, not which metric counts it. An event that feeds no credit-consuming metric is rejected with 422 — that usage belongs on POST /events; an event feeding several credit-consuming metrics is checked (and held) against all of them at once. Optional when events carries the sample; required for reserve.max_quantity.

options.name: ttl-seconds
options.description: How long the hold stays open, in seconds. Defaults to 900 (15 minutes) and cannot exceed 14400 (4 hours), the maximum lifetime any hold may reach. Use it for a run that cannot report progress as it goes; a run that can should send partial settlements to /track instead, since each one slides this same TTL forward. Requires reserve. Not part of idempotency identity: a retry under the same Idempotency-Key replays the original hold with its original expires_at, whatever ttl_seconds it now carries.

methods.name: get-reservation
methods.description:
Reports a reservation's current state, what it covers, and every close already committed against it.

`closes` exists for one recovery: a client that has lost its `Idempotency-Key` and cannot reproduce the events it sent can read what already landed, instead of resending and burning twice. This is a read and cannot settle anything. An unknown or foreign token returns `404`, indistinguishably.

methods.name: track
methods.description:
Records usage and charges credit for it. The request carries no credit amount: send what happened, and the response's `charges` carry what it priced to per metric, with `totals` as the sum.

Two shapes. A direct draw (`account` + `events`) charges against the account's current credit. A settlement (`reservation_id` + `events` + `close`) closes a hold opened by `/credits/check`, pricing each metric at the rate frozen when the hold opened. One payload can feed several credit-consuming metrics, and the draw is all-or-nothing: a refusal for one metric leaves every metric uncharged.

Events sent here are both metered and charged, so do not also send them to `POST /events`. An event feeding no credit-consuming metric is rejected with `422` and belongs there instead. Insufficient credit returns `200` with `allowed: false`.

The events' own `unique_id`s identify the work, so a resent batch draws once. The SDKs send no automatic `Idempotency-Key` on this call and retry it without one. Send your own key only to replay a specific response; it then replaces the `unique_id`s as the identity, so reuse it when you resend the same work. The SDKs do not retry a `500`. `409` means the identity is bound to different work. Back off on `429`.

options.name: account
options.description: Customer account ID or alias; direct-draw mode. Required unless reservation_id is set, where the account comes from the reservation.

options.name: close
options.description: Whether this is the final call for the reservation. Required whenever reservation_id is set: there is no safe default, since true would end runs that meant to continue and false would leak reservations until they expire. The reservation also closes on its own if the events consume everything held. Not valid on a direct draw.

options.name: on-envelope-exceeded
options.description: What to do when a settle cannot be fully covered by credit on a metric that stops at zero — either because it prices past the reservation's authorized hold, or because credit ran out before a late settle arrived. "reject" (the default) refuses the settle, burning and recording nothing. "record" burns what is available and reports the remainder in the charges' overflow, deliberately weakening a hard stop you configured. Reservation-settlement mode only. The refusal body's reason says which condition fired: adding credit resolves coverage_shortfall, but not envelope_exceeded, whose limit is the hold's size.

options.name: reservation-id
options.description: Reservation token returned by /check, to close it; reservation-settlement mode. Mutually exclusive with account. The events sent alongside are both metered and charged, so do not send them to /events as well.

commands.name: customers
commands.description: The accounts you bill, with their connected accounts and entitlements.

methods.name: list
methods.description: Returns a paginated list of customers. Supports filtering by sales owner, customer success manager, tag IDs, active-subscription status, integration IDs, alias, and contact email.

options.name: alias
options.description: Filter by customer alias (external ID)

options.name: csm-id
options.description: Filter by customer success manager user ID (comma-separated to match any)

options.name: email
options.description: Filter by contact email address

options.name: has-active-subscriptions
options.description: Filter by whether the customer has active subscriptions

options.name: integration-ids
options.description: Filter by external integration IDs (comma-separated to match any)

options.name: limit
options.description: Number of items to return per page

options.name: offset
options.description: Number of items to skip

options.name: sales-owner-id
options.description: Filter by sales owner user ID (comma-separated to match any)

options.name: sort
options.description: Sort field and direction in format field:order. Sortable fields: name, created_at

options.name: tag-ids
options.description: Filter by tag IDs (comma-separated to match any)

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates a new customer with optional contacts, billing address, aliases, and a required default currency.

options.name: currency
options.description: ISO 4217 currency code

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the customer

methods.name: lookup
methods.summary: Look up a customer ID by alias
methods.description: Resolves an alias to its Alguna customer ID. The `alias` accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID). Returns 404 if no customer in your organization matches. Use this when you hold an external identifier and only need the Alguna ID; to fetch the full customer, use Get a customer instead.

options.name: alias
options.description: Customer alias to resolve — an Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID)

methods.name: get
methods.description: Fetches a single customer by ID, including contacts, billing address, and tax details (rate, status, country, type, and taxability reason). The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID).

methods.name: update
methods.description: Patches an existing customer. Only the fields provided in the request body are modified. Supplying contacts or aliases replaces the full list. The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID).

options.name: currency
options.description: ISO 4217 currency code

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the customer

methods.name: list-connected-accounts
methods.summary: List connected accounts for a customer
methods.description: Returns the customer's accounts in connected external systems (for example a Stripe customer or a HubSpot company), including the integration each link belongs to, the account's identifier in the external system, and a link to it where available. The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID).

methods.name: create-connected-account
methods.summary: Link a connected account to a customer
methods.description: Links the customer to an account in an external system by recording the integration and the account's identifier in that system. This records the mapping only: it does not create anything in the external system and does not trigger a sync of any data in either direction. The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or an existing connected-account external ID.

options.name: external-id
options.description: Identifier of the account in the external system

options.name: integration-id
options.description: Identifier of the integration to link the account through

methods.name: delete-connected-account
methods.summary: Unlink a connected account from a customer
methods.description: Removes the link between the customer and an external-system account. This removes the mapping only: it does not delete anything in the external system and does not trigger a sync. The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or an existing connected-account external ID.
methods.requireConfirmation: This operation unlinks the external account from the customer. It changes nothing in the external system.

methods.name: list-entitlements
methods.summary: List active entitlements for a customer
methods.description: Returns the flattened list of active entitlements across all of the customer's active subscriptions. Each entry is a single entitlement on the current published version of one active subscription. Use the `subscription_id` field on each entry to see which subscription the entitlement comes from. The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID).

methods.name: list-payment-methods
methods.summary: List saved payment methods for a customer
methods.description: Returns the customer's saved, active payment methods, newest first, with redacted details only: card brand, last four digits and expiry, or the last four digits of a bank account. `is_default` marks the payment method that auto-pay charges when a subscription has no payment method of its own. Payment methods saved through a checkout session with `checkout_intent: vault` appear here once the customer completes the session. The `id` path parameter accepts the Alguna account ID, a customer alias, or a connected-account external ID (such as a Stripe customer ID).

commands.name: events
commands.description: Billable usage events, which metered prices read.

methods.name: ingest
methods.description: Ingests a batch of usage events for metering. Accepts up to 100 events per request. Each event must carry a unique `unique_id` for idempotency and may include arbitrary properties used by metric filters and aggregations.

commands.name: insights
commands.description: Revenue, billings, customer and receivables reports.

methods.name: ar-aging
methods.description: Returns the organization-wide receivables position as of now: total open balance, the past-due portion, invoice counts, and a breakdown by days past due. Unlike the other insights endpoints this is a point-in-time snapshot rather than a period aggregate, so it takes no date range. Amounts from every currency are converted into the organization's base currency.

methods.name: ar-aging-by-customer
methods.summary: Get accounts receivable aging by customer
methods.description: Returns one entry per customer and currency, each with the open balance, invoice counts, and a breakdown by days past due. A customer billed in more than one currency produces one entry per currency, so entries for a single customer can be summed by invoice count but never by amount. Like the aging summary, this is a point-in-time snapshot and takes no date range.

options.name: customer-alias
options.description: Filter by an alternative identifier (external ID) for the customer. Used when customer_id is not provided.

options.name: customer-id
options.description: Filter by customer ID. Provide at most one of customer_id or customer_alias; omit both to report on every customer.

methods.name: billings-by-customer

options.name: date-range

options.name: customer-id

options.name: date-range

methods.name: customers-over-time
methods.description: Returns a time series of customer lifecycle events: new, reactivated, existing, and churned customer counts per period.

options.name: date-range
options.description: Time period for the query. Determines the primary period and automatically calculates a comparison period.

methods.name: revenue

methods.name: revenue-breakdown-over-time

methods.name: revenue-by-customer
methods.description: Returns top customers ranked by net revenue for the selected period, with a comparison to the prior period. Remaining customers are aggregated into an 'other' total.

options.name: date-range
options.description: Time period for the query. Determines the primary period and automatically calculates a comparison period.

options.name: customer-id

methods.description: Returns a time series of net revenue data points split into fixed and metered components. Resolution (daily or monthly) is automatically determined by the date range.

options.name: date-range
options.description: Time period for the query. Determines the primary period and automatically calculates a comparison period.

methods.name: revenue-by-subscription
methods.summary: Get MRR, ARR, and ACV for a subscription

options.description: Filter by tax calculation ID

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates an ad-hoc invoice for a customer. Callers can supply line items, a billing period, purchase order number, and an initial status (`draft` or `issued`). Requesting `issued` releases the invoice for issuance, which completes asynchronously — the response returns the invoice in `processing` and it settles to `issued` shortly after, observable via the Get Invoice endpoint. Alternatively, pass `tax_calculation_id` to turn a persisted tax calculation into an invoice: its line items, tax, and buyer are pinned and the invoice is issued synchronously; add a `payment` and `status: paid` to record settlement and mark it paid in the same call.

options.name: billing-period-end
options.description: End of the invoice's billing period, exclusive: for a period through 31 January send 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z. Send with billing_period_start.

options.name: billing-period-start
options.description: Start of the invoice's billing period, inclusive. Send with billing_period_end.

options.name: currency
options.description: ISO 4217 currency code; required unless tax_calculation_id is set

options.name: customer-id
options.description: Existing customer to bill. On the tax_calculation_id path, leave empty to mint a guest customer from the calculation's buyer.

options.name: description
options.description: Invoice description or memo

options.name: issue-date
options.description: Date to issue the invoice

options.name: merchant-id
options.description: Existing sub-merchant the invoice is issued for; you remain the seller of record. Create the merchant before referencing it here. Optional alongside tax_calculation_id, where it must match the merchant the calculation was made for. Requires the merchants entitlement

options.name: purchase-order-number
options.description: Purchase order number

options.name: status
options.description: Initial invoice status. Defaults to draft. Setting issued releases the invoice for issuance, which completes asynchronously: the response returns the invoice in processing, and it settles to issued shortly after — poll the Get Invoice endpoint to observe the final status. paid is only valid on the tax_calculation_id path and must be sent together with a payment.

options.name: tax-calculation-id
options.description: Id of a persisted tax calculation; its stored line items, tax amounts, and buyer become the invoice, which is issued synchronously with no recalculation. Mutually exclusive with line_items (the calculation supplies them). Leave status unset or set it to issued to issue the invoice; set status to paid together with a payment to also mark it paid.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Fetches a single invoice by ID, including all line items, totals, and status.

methods.name: update
methods.description: Patches descriptive metadata on an existing invoice (description, purchase order number). Line items are managed through the dedicated line item endpoints.

options.name: description
options.description: Invoice description or memo

options.name: purchase-order-number
options.description: Purchase order number

methods.name: add-line-item
methods.description: Adds a new line item to an existing invoice. The invoice must not yet be finalized.

options.name: billing-period-end
options.description: End of the service period this line covers, exclusive: for a period through 31 January send 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z. Send with billing_period_start.

options.name: billing-period-start
options.description: Start of the service period this line covers, inclusive. Send with billing_period_end.

options.name: description
options.description: Description of the line item

options.name: quantity
options.description: Quantity

options.name: unit-price
options.description: Unit price, excluding tax. Tax is calculated on top of it.

methods.name: delete-line-item
methods.description: Removes a line item from an invoice. The invoice must not yet be finalized.
methods.requireConfirmation: This operation removes the line item from the invoice.

methods.name: update-line-item
methods.description: Patches an existing invoice line item. Only the fields provided in the request body are modified.

options.name: description
options.description: Description of the line item

methods.name: mark-as-paid
methods.description: Records a manual payment against an invoice. Accepts an optional amount (defaults to the invoice total), payment date, external payment source, and free-text note. Transitions the invoice to `paid` when the balance is settled.

options.name: amount-paid
options.description: Amount paid; defaults to the full invoice total

options.name: external-payment-note
options.description: Free-text note about the payment

options.name: external-payment-source
options.description: Payment source

options.name: paid-date
options.description: Date of payment; defaults to the current date

methods.requireConfirmation: This operation records a manual payment against the invoice. It cannot be reversed.

methods.name: generate-pdf
methods.description: Returns the rendered PDF for an invoice as a binary `application/pdf` response. If a custom PDF has been uploaded for the invoice, it is served directly, otherwise the standard template is rendered on demand.
methods.epilogue:
Example:
  alguna invoices generate-pdf inv_123 --out invoice.pdf

methods.name: void
methods.description: Voids an invoice, marking it as no longer collectable. Accepts an optional void date (defaults to the current date); it may be backdated but must not be in the future or before the invoice's issue date. Only issued or overdue invoices can be voided: voiding an invoice in any other status returns a 400, and an out-of-range void date returns a 422.

options.name: void-date
options.description: Date the invoice was voided; defaults to the current date. May be backdated but must not be in the future or before the invoice's issue date.

methods.requireConfirmation: This operation voids the invoice, so it can no longer be collected. It cannot be reversed.

commands.name: merchants
commands.description: The merchants that issue your invoices and quotes, with their branding.

methods.name: list
methods.description: Returns a paginated list of merchants, by display name. Archived merchants are excluded unless you ask for them.

options.name: display-name
options.description: Return only merchants with these display names, comma-separated. Matched exactly, including case.

options.name: external-id

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates a quote, in `draft`. A new-business quote starts from a plan, duplicates an existing subscription using `source_subscription_id`, or starts from a blank canvas with `items` (single phase) or `phases` (ramp); its phases are read and edited under `/quotes/{id}/phases` until the quote is activated. An amendment quote names the active subscription it amends (`amends_subscription_id`) and carries the changed phase in `phases`; it may be issued immediately, so branch on `status` and read `signing_url` when it is present.

options.name: amends-subscription-id
options.description: Amend this active subscription. Takes exactly one entry in phases, with a start_date, and no other origin.

options.name: auto-activate
options.description: Whether the subscription takes effect on its own once signed: a new-business quote activates at its contract start, an amendment applies immediately. Defaults to the plan's or organization's setting for new business, and to true for an amendment; each quote keeps its own value.

options.name: customer-id
options.description: Customer ID. For an amendment, must be the subscription's customer.

options.name: expires-at
options.description: When the signing offer lapses. Defaults to the organization's quote expiry window.

options.name: name
options.description: Names the subscription a blank-canvas quote creates. Only valid when neither plan_id nor source_subscription_id is provided; a plan or duplicate names itself.

options.name: plan-id
options.description: Seed the quote from a plan. The quote inherits the plan's pricing. Mutually exclusive with source_subscription_id and price_book_id.

options.name: price-book-id
options.description: Price book a blank-canvas quote draws its pricing from. Mutually exclusive with plan_id and source_subscription_id.

options.name: source-subscription-id
options.description: Duplicate an existing subscription into a new quote. Mutually exclusive with plan_id and price_book_id.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Returns a quote, including its `signing_url` while a customer signature is pending. Whether the deal is in effect is the state of `subscription_id`, not of the quote: a signed quote stays `signed`, so read that subscription to see activation.

methods.name: discard
methods.description: Deletes a draft quote and the draft subscription it documents, for a quote that was abandoned before anyone saw it. Requires `status` of `draft` and a new-business quote: once sent, a quote is a document someone may hold, so it is withdrawn rather than erased.
methods.requireConfirmation: This operation deletes the draft quote and its draft subscription.

methods.name: update
methods.description: Updates a quote's name override and its signing deadline. The override names the quote, not the subscription; subscription content is edited through the quote's phases.

options.name: clear-expires-at
options.description: Make the signing offer open-ended.

options.name: clear-name
options.description: Drop the override, falling back to the subscription's name.

options.name: expires-at
options.description: Move the signing deadline. Ignored when clear_expires_at is true.

options.name: name
options.description: Name override for this quote. Does not rename the subscription. Ignored when clear_name is true.

methods.name: activate
methods.description: Puts a signed quote into effect: requires `status` of `signed`. A new-business quote activates its subscription; an amendment publishes its phase onto the live subscription. Quotes with `auto_activate` take effect on their own once signed (a new-business quote at its contract start), so this is only needed for manual activation. The quote itself stays `signed` — read `subscription_id` to confirm the deal is live.

methods.name: mark-signed-offline
methods.summary: Mark a quote as signed offline
methods.description: Records a signature captured outside the hosted signing page, for consumers that collect signer consent through their own e-sign flow. Accepts a `draft` quote, issuing it first so no live Alguna signing link has to be created for a document signed elsewhere, or one already `sent`. The quote moves to `signed` and the subscription to `accepted`, exactly as a hosted signature would. When issuing a `draft` quote needs approval, the call fails with the pending approval flow and records no signature; after approval issues the quote, call this again with a signature that applies to the issued terms. `signed_at` must lie between the quote's creation and now.

options.name: signed-at
options.description: When the signer consented, as captured by your e-sign flow. Defaults to now.

options.name: signer-email
options.description: Signer's email.

options.name: signer-name
options.description: Full name of the signer.

options.name: signer-role
options.description: Signer's job title.

methods.name: get-pdf
methods.description: Returns the quote document as a binary `application/pdf` response: the PDF the customer signed, or the currently issued one while the quote is out for signature. Returns `404` when there is no issued document — a quote still in `draft`, or a withdrawn amendment, whose staged phase the withdrawal discarded.

methods.name: list-phases
methods.description: Returns the priced phases a quote proposes, in schedule order, each with its revenue totals. An amendment quote has the single phase it was issued for. `sequence` is the position in that order, not an identifier — deleting a phase renumbers the rest, so address a phase by its `id`. Each phase is the subscription version it becomes: once the quote is signed the same rows are readable on the subscription.

methods.name: create-phase
methods.description: Stages a further priced phase on a new-business quote that has not been signed. Name its start as a date or as months after the billing start.

options.name: description
options.description: Human-readable note on the phase

options.name: start-date
options.description: When the phase starts (YYYY-MM-DD). Alternative to start_month_offset.

options.name: start-month-offset
options.description: Months after the billing start when the phase begins; resolved into a date at signature. Alternative to start_date.

methods.name: get-phase
methods.description: Returns one of the quote's phases with its revenue totals.

methods.name: replace-phase
methods.description: Replaces the items and start of one of the quote's draft phases. Send the complete item set; items you omit are removed. Phases publish when the quote is sent and cannot change after that.

options.name: description
options.description: Human-readable note on the phase

options.name: start-date
options.description: When the phase starts (YYYY-MM-DD). Alternative to start_month_offset.

options.name: start-month-offset
options.description: Months after the billing start when the phase begins; resolved into a date at signature. Alternative to start_date.

methods.name: delete-phase
methods.description: Discards one of the quote's draft phases. Phases publish when the quote is sent and cannot be deleted after that.
methods.requireConfirmation: This operation deletes the draft quote phase.

methods.name: list-phase-items
methods.description: Returns the priced items of one of the quote's phases.

methods.name: send-for-signature
methods.description: Issues a quote revision (snapshot + rendered PDF) and moves the quote to `sent`, returning it with the `signing_url` for the customer to review and sign. Requires `draft`, `rejected` or `pending_approval`, and only a new-business quote: an amendment is issued when it is created. Omit `signer_email` to send no invitation and share the link yourself. When issuing needs approval, the call fails with the pending approval flow and the quote is not issued until that approval completes; repeating the call meanwhile returns the same pending flow.

options.name: signer-email
options.description: Email the signing link is sent to. When omitted no email is sent; share signing_url yourself.

options.name: signer-name
options.description: Name of the person expected to sign, recorded on the signature session.

options.name: signer-role
options.description: Signer's job title, recorded on the signature session.

methods.name: withdraw
methods.description: Cancels a quote that is out for signature: requires `status` of `sent`. Withdrawing a new-business quote withdraws its subscription and keeps the issued document; withdrawing an amendment discards the staged draft phase, so its document no longer renders. Use Discard a draft quote for one that was never sent.

options.description: Optional reason recorded on the withdrawal.

methods.requireConfirmation: This operation withdraws the quote, so the customer can no longer sign it. It cannot be reversed.

methods.description: Creates a new version from a complete item set. Returns a draft by default that can be edited and published later. This is the snapshot-based mutation path (Path B) for full control over the version contents. For the delta-based alternative, use the Apply Changes to a Subscription endpoint. See the [Updating a Subscription](https://alguna.com/docs/api-reference/v2/examples/updating-a-subscription) examples.

options.name: description
options.description: Human-readable audit note

options.name: draft
options.description: Create as draft (true) or auto-publish (false, default)

options.name: effective-at
options.description: When the version takes effect (ISO 8601 date, YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.

methods.name: get-current
methods.summary: Get the current active subscription version
methods.description: Returns the subscription version that is currently in effect. This is the published version whose start date has passed and whose end date is either in the future or null. Returns 404 if the subscription has no active published version.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Fetches a single version by ID, including its priced items and entitlements.

methods.name: replace
methods.description: Replaces the contents of a draft version in place. Snapshot-based: send the full intended item set. Items you omit are removed. Only draft versions can be replaced, published versions are immutable. See the [Updating a Subscription](https://alguna.com/docs/api-reference/v2/examples/updating-a-subscription) examples.

options.name: description
options.description: Human-readable audit note

options.name: effective-at
options.description: Updated effective date (ISO 8601 date, YYYY-MM-DD)

methods.name: delete
methods.description: Discards an unwanted draft version. Published versions are immutable historical records and cannot be deleted, they must be superseded by creating a new version instead. See the [Updating a Subscription](https://alguna.com/docs/api-reference/v2/examples/updating-a-subscription) examples.
methods.requireConfirmation: This operation deletes the draft subscription version.

methods.name: get-item
methods.description: Fetches a single priced item from a version, addressed by either its product ID or its bundle ID. Bundle items return every child with its price.

methods.name: publish
methods.description: Publishes a draft version. If `effective_at` is in the past or today the version becomes the current active version immediately. Otherwise it sits as a pending change on the parent subscription until the effective date. See the [Updating a Subscription](https://alguna.com/docs/api-reference/v2/examples/updating-a-subscription) examples.

methods.name: get-revenue
methods.summary: Get subscription revenue metrics for a specific version
methods.description: Returns the monthly recurring revenue (MRR), annual recurring revenue (ARR), and annual contract value (ACV) computed from the pricing on the specified subscription version. This is the same calculation used in the Alguna dashboard subscription builder, so results match what is shown there one-to-one.

commands.name: tax
commands.description: Tax calculations.

methods.name: list-calculations
methods.description: Returns a paginated list of stored calculations, newest first, for reconciling what was quoted against what was issued. Each entry carries the total tax, whether the calculation was issued from and into which invoice, and whether it can still be issued from. Supports filtering by customer reference, currency, issued and expired state, and a tax date range. Per-line tax is on the get endpoint, not here.

options.name: consumed
options.description: Filter by whether an invoice has been issued from the calculation

options.name: currency
options.description: Filter by currency. Pass a comma-separated list to match any.

options.name: customer-reference
options.description: Filter by your own buyer id. Pass a comma-separated list to match any.

options.name: expired
options.description: Filter by whether the calculation can still be issued from

options.name: limit
options.description: Number of items to return per page

options.name: offset
options.description: Number of items to skip

options.name: sort
options.description: Sort field and direction in format field:order. Sortable fields: created_at, tax_date, expires_at, total_tax, currency.

options.name: tax-date-gte
options.description: Tax date lower bound (inclusive)

options.name: tax-date-lte
options.description: Tax date upper bound (inclusive)

methods.name: create-calculation
methods.description: Computes tax for inline line items against your legal entity's configured tax engine and stores the result, returning an id (with an expiry) you pass when issuing a receipt to pin these exact line items and amounts. Each call creates a new calculation; send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry return the original calculation instead of a new one. Provide a buyer address (and optional tax ids for reverse-charge / exemption) and per-line canonical tax codes; an omitted code defaults to general business SaaS.
methods.epilogue:
Example (calculation.json sets currency, customer and line_items):
  alguna tax create-calculation --body @calculation.json

options.name: currency
options.description: ISO 4217 currency code

options.name: legal-entity-id
options.description: Selling legal entity; defaults to the org's default when omitted

options.name: merchant-id
options.description: Existing sub-merchant the receipt is issued for; you remain the seller of record. Create the merchant before referencing it here. Requires the merchants entitlement

options.name: tax-behavior
options.description: Whether line amounts exclude (default) or already include tax

methods.name: get-calculation
methods.description: Returns one stored calculation: the lines as they were submitted joined with the engine's answer for each, plus the invoice it was issued into when it has been. A calculation stays readable after it expires or is issued from, so this is the audit record behind an invoice's tax. Read it back with the `tax_calculation_id` returned on the invoice.
